name: settings-form
title: Settings Form
author: @fma-ds/ds
description:
A long edit form in sections, saved as a whole (account, company, preferences).

- **`SettingsForm`**: a react-aria `Form` that only shows state the app owns, so react-hook-form or any other form state fits: `isDirty` (enables Save and Discard), `isPending` (spinner on Save, `aria-busy`) and `onReset` (adds a Discard button that should restore the saved values). Without `isDirty`, for uncontrolled fields, the form compares its data with the data it started with (fields need a `name`) and Discard resets them to their defaults; after saving, give the form a new `key` so the saved values become the defaults.
- **`SettingsSection`**: groups fields under a `title` and `description` (a labelled group) stacked above them, leaving the width to the fields next to an app sidebar. The fields fall into a two-column grid when there's room (container query); `col-span-full` takes the whole row.
- **`SettingsFormFooter`**: a save bar stuck to the bottom of the viewport with a polite status line (no changes / unsaved / saving), optional children before the buttons, Discard and Save. With the form on a `Card`, put the `SettingsForm` around the card (the buttons stay in the form) and put the bar in a sticky `CardFooter` with `framed={false}`, which drops its own bar.

Warning before leaving with unsaved changes stays in the app, since it depends on the router; use `confirm-dialog`.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`.
